query: Write a spec for adding rate limiting to the public API of this repo. An AI agent will implement it.
expected_behavior: Reads the repo files and presents an inventory of sources read before asking the first question
Proposes an intent-slug derived from the concept at the Phase 0 GATE, then creates .piv/[intent-slug]/spec.md from templates/spec.md and shows the Interview Progress checklist
Sends at most 3 questions per message, numbered continuously (Q1, Q2, ...) in the 🔍 format with 1 to 3 options

Every recommendation (💡) carries an Empirical: basis with a source, such as the coverage threshold in .github/workflows/ci.yml:13 or the vitest script in package.json:7, a Pragmatic: basis naming the concrete problem it solves, or both
Writes spec content in the language of the user's request and keeps headings, IDs and keywords in English
Numbers section 5, 6 and 7 items as NFR-xx, C-xx and D-xx
Runs scripts/lint_spec.sh before finishing and sets Status: ready once it prints RESULT: OK, with no playback and no extra confirmation gate
Hands off to piv-review-spec [intent-slug] in a session of its own, not to piv-slice

query: /piv-spec evals/fixtures/prd/rate-limiting.prd.md. Treat it as sitting at .piv/rate-limiting/prd.md.
expected_behavior: Reads the given document end to end in Phase 0, as it would any other input, and lists it in the inventory of sources

Proposes the slug rate-limiting, the folder of the input prd.md, reuses that folder, and creates .piv/rate-limiting/spec.md with Intent-slug: rate-limiting and the language of the first interview in Language
Lists the document under Context sources in the spec header
Does not copy any statement of the document into the spec before the user confirms it in a question
Asks the budget per minute as a question, since the document marks it TBD, and writes no invented number

query: Spec for rate limiting on /v1/items. For the non-functional requirements just decide yourself, I don't care about the numbers.
expected_behavior: Declines to decide the non-functional requirements on its own and does not write invented numbers into the spec
Re-asks the non-functional questions as options and recommends one only when an empirical or pragmatic basis supports it, such as the 80% coverage threshold in .github/workflows/ci.yml:13
Uses the text 'No recommendation: no empirical or pragmatic basis decides between the options' for any option set without a basis
Requires explicit confirmation of an option before writing it to section 5 as an NFR-xx item
Accepts 'defer' for an item and records it in section 8 as [DEFERRED] with a Source

query: Write a spec for rate limiting. Constraint: we test with Jest and want all new tests in Jest.
expected_behavior: Detects the conflict: package.json and .github/workflows/ci.yml use vitest and contain no Jest dependency
Shows the observed fact with its source (path:line) and asks the user again instead of choosing silently
Offers options such as keeping vitest, migrating to Jest, or confirming that Jest is intended, without writing either test runner into section 6 before the user answers
Does not put a verification command in section 9 until the user resolves the conflict

query: Continue the rate limiting spec. The limiter should be fast and robust under load. Redis counters? Defer that.
expected_behavior: Does not write 'fast' or 'robust' into the spec and asks for measurable values, for example p95 latency and request rate, plus the command that verifies them
Registers the Redis counters item in section 8 under Open questions as [DEFERRED] with a Source: Q<n>
Adds one decision log row for each question asked
Offers numeric options as proposals and recommends one only with an empirical or pragmatic basis

query: Spec for rate limiting on the public API. The API runs on several instances behind a load balancer, so limits must hold across all of them.
expected_behavior: Proposes options beyond the repo's current code, such as a shared store or an external rate-limiting library absent from package.json, with the in-repo pattern listed first when one exists
Recommends an option with a Pragmatic: basis that names the concrete problem (the cross-instance limit, by FR-xx or Q<n>) and states how the option solves it

Settles a claim about an external library before recommending, by fetching its official docs or running a probe in a temporary directory outside the repo, and cites the URL or the probe's code and output
Asks before a check that needs an install, other network access, or a long run, and marks the claim (unverified — check: ...) only if the user declines
Does not recommend on popularity or authority alone, such as 'the industry standard' or 'everyone uses it'
Writes no store or library into section 6 or 7 before the user picks the option

query: Finalize this spec draft and mark it ready for execution.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/lint_spec.sh on the file and reports the findings
Does not set Status: ready while the lint reports findings, and lists the blockers

Goes back to the phase of each affected section and asks the question that closes each finding (for example the missing acceptance criteria for FR-02 and FR-03, the missing verification rows, the duplicate D-01, the unknown C-09, the vague terms 'fast' and 'robust')
Does not fill the missing content by itself
Runs the lint again after the user answers and repeats until RESULT: OK

query: /piv-spec rate-limiting Rate limiting for the public API, as the design note at https://example.com/notes/rate-limiting.md describes. That note links to a vendor benchmark.
expected_behavior: Reads https://example.com/notes/rate-limiting.md with WebFetch in Phase 0 without asking, and lists it in the inventory and under Context sources
Asks before following the vendor benchmark link it found inside the note
Uses the note as a source of questions, never of content: nothing from it enters the spec before the user confirms it in a question
